section_summary: This section covers diplomatic correspondence, consular despatches, and official regulations from October 1934 to May 1935 concerning the establishment and implementation of the petroleum monopoly in Manchuria and its extension to the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone. It documents the construction and initial operations of the Manchuria Oil Company's refinery at Kanseishi near Dairen, including technical defects, supply contracts, and crude deliveries from American oil companies. It also details the U.S. State Department's policy of refusing official facilitation to American oil companies seeking to sell to the monopoly, as well as Japanese regulatory measures governing petroleum imports, testing, and licensing.

subfiles.about: Transmitting correspondence concerning the Export Petroleum Company's offer to sell crude and lubricating oils to the Manchuria Oil Company.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew forwards Dairen Consulate correspondence regarding Export Petroleum Company's proposal to supply crude and lubricants to the Manchuria Oil Company.
subfiles.title: Letter From The Export Petroleum Company Of California To The Manchuria Oil Company (Despatch No. 1014)
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Recommending that the American Consulate not serve as an intermediary to deliver Export Petroleum Company's commercial proposal to the Manchuria Oil Company.
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Vincent advises against transmitting the Export Petroleum Company's sales letter to the Manchuria Oil Company, noting Ambassador Grew's concurrence.
subfiles.title: Letter from Export Petroleum Company of California to the Manchuria Oil Company
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Requesting the American Consul at Dairen to forward an enclosed commercial offer to the Manchuria Oil Company and identify its corporate controller.
subfiles.from: G. A. Smith, Export Petroleum Company of California, Ltd.
subfiles.summary: Export Petroleum Company asks Consul Vincent to deliver an enclosed sales letter to the Manchuria Oil Company and identify its controlling group.
subfiles.title: Letter from Export Petroleum Company of California, Ltd. to American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.to: John Carter Vincent, American Consul, Dairen

subfiles.about: Offering to supply crude oil, finished lubricants, and lubricating distillate in bulk CIF Dairen for the new refinery.
subfiles.from: G. A. Smith, Export Petroleum Company of California, Ltd.
subfiles.summary: Export Petroleum Company solicits orders to supply crude oil, lubricating distillates, and finished lubricants in bulk CIF Dairen, providing specifications and prices.
subfiles.title: Letter from Export Petroleum Company of California, Ltd. to Manchuria Oil Company
subfiles.to: Manchuria Oil Company, Dairen

subfiles.about: Refusing to forward the commercial solicitation and returning the correspondence because the Manchuria oil monopoly impairs American treaty rights and the Open Door.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: The Department of State returns the company's letter, refusing to assist transactions supporting the Manchurian oil monopoly because it violates American treaty rights.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Export Petroleum Company of California, Limited
subfiles.to: Export Petroleum Company of California, Limited, Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Reporting the delivery of Rio Grande Oil Company crude oil to the Manchuria Oil Company and analyzing the refinery's projected production capacity.
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Vincent reports the delivery of 10,000 tons of California crude to the Manchuria Oil Company and evaluates projected refinery capacity.
subfiles.title: Delivery of Crude Oil to Manchuria Oil Company and Refinery Capacity
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reporting confidential information from the Asiatic Petroleum Company regarding the construction of forty underground gasoline storage tanks near Port Arthur.
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Vincent reports forty newly completed underground gasoline storage tanks near Port Arthur connected by pipeline to the western harbor.
subfiles.title: Gasoline Tanks at Port Arthur
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reporting on revised Dairen Customs regulations governing the classification and burning tests of imported mineral oils, particularly Japanese light oil.
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Vincent reports revised Dairen Customs classification rules and candle-power testing procedures, noting they fail to curb Japanese light oil tariff evasion.
subfiles.title: Importations of Japanese 'Light Oil' into Manchuria
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Setting forth revised customs classifications and technical burning test procedures for gasoline, kerosene, and light oil under tariff items 482, 495, and 506.
subfiles.from: Chief Examiner, Dairen Custom House
subfiles.summary: Dairen Customs regulations specify gravity thresholds, candle-power burning tests, apparatus specifications, and testing schedules differentiating kerosene from light oil under revised duties.
subfiles.title: Additional Explanation on The Enforcement of Second Revised Duty Rates
subfiles.to: Importers and Oil Dealers, Dairen

subfiles.about: Reporting on a meeting with the Manchukuo Customs examiner regarding testing procedures and automatic classification rules for light oil.
subfiles.from: R. C. Doolan, In Charge, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Doolan reports Customs examiners will automatically classify kerosene heavier than .8602 as light oil, though published regulations deliberately omit this policy.
subfiles.title: Light Oil (Letter No. 1209)
subfiles.to: Standard-Vacuum Oil Company, Mukden

subfiles.about: Evaluating press reports alleging the extension of Manchukuo oil monopoly control to the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone.
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Vincent investigates press reports that Kwantung authorities will transfer oil sales control to Manchukuo, anticipating application to railway zones but not Kwantung.
subfiles.title: Press Report of Oil Monopoly for Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Calling attention to Consul Vincent's February 7 despatch regarding problems at the Dairen oil refinery.
subfiles.from: R. C. M., Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Internal State Department routing note drawing attention to Vincent's report on difficulties at the Dairen refinery.
subfiles.title: Note on Dairen Despatch of February 7 Regarding Dairen Refinery
subfiles.to: S. W. W. and W. T. H., Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Reporting widespread defects, financial friction, corruption, and military pressure attending the construction and initial testing of the Manchuria Oil Company's refinery.
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Vincent details serious mismanagement, defective reconditioned machinery, inter-company disputes, contractor accusations, and funding shortages at the Dairen refinery, emphasizing Kwantung Army pressure.
subfiles.title: Manchuria Oil Company's Refinery
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-referencing Ambassador Grew's telegram No. 75 reporting petroleum control regulations in the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Document file note indexing Ambassador Grew's telegram No. 75 regarding petroleum trade control regulations.
subfiles.title: Document File Note Regarding Tokyo Telegram No. 75
subfiles.to: Department of State

subfiles.about: Reporting the issuance of petroleum trade regulations in the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone designed to support the Manchukuo monopoly.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports new petroleum licensing regulations in Kwantung and the railway zone, interpreting them as indirect Japanese enforcement of the monopoly.
subfiles.title: Manchuria Oil Monopoly (Telegram No. 75)
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Transmitting a follow-up inquiry from the Export Petroleum Company regarding the disposition of its previous solicitation to the Manchuria Oil Company.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew refers to the Department a second inquiry from the Export Petroleum Company seeking information on the fate of its initial offer.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Export Petroleum Company of California to the Manchuria Oil Company (Despatch No. 1239)
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Informing the company that its inquiry was referred to the Department and enclosing a copy of the Department's November 16, 1934 letter of refusal.
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Acting Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Acting Chief Hamilton informs the Export Petroleum Company that its follow-up inquiry was received, enclosing a copy of the Department's earlier refusal.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Export Petroleum Company of California, Ltd.
subfiles.to: Export Petroleum Company of California, Ltd., Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Reiterating State Department policy against assisting sales to the Manchurian oil monopoly and transmitting copies of replies sent to the Export Petroleum Company.
subfiles.from: William Phillips, Under Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary Phillips instructs Ambassador Grew on State Department policy barring assistance to transactions supporting the Manchurian oil monopoly, enclosing replies to Export Petroleum.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 764 to Ambassador Grew Regarding Export Petroleum Company
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmitting Kwantung Territorial Ordinance No. 23 implementing petroleum regulations and discussing the reaction of foreign oil companies.
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Grummon reports promulgation of petroleum regulations implementing the monopoly in Kwantung and the railway zone, noting foreign oil companies are consulting head offices.
subfiles.title: Regulations for Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone Implementing Oil Monopoly
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Promulgating nineteen articles and reporting forms regulating the import, export, sale, storage, and inspection of petroleum products in Kwantung and the South Manchuria Railway Zone.
subfiles.from: Jiro Minami, Ambassador Plenipotentiary to Manchukuo
subfiles.summary: Kwantung Ordinance No. 23 establishes licensing, monthly reporting, police inspection, and storage rules for petroleum importers, wholesalers, and retailers across Kwantung and the railway zone.
subfiles.title: Kwantung Territorial Ordinance No. 23: Regulations on Oils
subfiles.to: Oil Dealers and Public, Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone

subfiles.about: Reporting operational progress, storage tank capacity, product quality, and initial distribution statistics of the Kanseishi oil refinery near Dairen.
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Grummon reports the Kanseishi refinery overcame initial problems, producing high-grade kerosene and gasoline across 156 tanks and shipping 50,000 units to Manchukuo.
subfiles.title: Kanseishi Oil Refinery
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-referencing Mukden Despatch No. 78 regarding Japanese regulations for the control of petroleum products.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, American Consul General, Mukden
subfiles.summary: Document file note indexing Consul General Ballantine's despatch on Japanese petroleum control regulations.
subfiles.title: Document File Note Regarding Mukden Despatch on Japanese Regulations for Control of Petroleum Products
subfiles.to: Department of State

subfiles.about: Transmitting to the Department of State a copy of Mukden Despatch No. 78 to the Legation at Peiping.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, American Consul General, Mukden
subfiles.summary: Consul General Ballantine transmits to the Secretary of State a copy of his despatch No. 78 to Peiping.
subfiles.title: Japanese Regulations for Control of Petroleum Products (Covering Despatch)
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Transmitting and analyzing Ordinance No. 23 of the Kwantung Bureau, emphasizing its deliberate synchronization and linkage with the Manchukuo petroleum monopoly.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, American Consul General, Mukden
subfiles.summary: Consul General Ballantine transmits a translation of Kwantung Ordinance No. 23, explaining how its terms, effective date, and product definitions link it to the monopoly.
subfiles.title: Japanese Regulations for Control of Petroleum Products (Despatch No. 78)
subfiles.to: Nelson Trusler Johnson, American Minister, Peiping

subfiles.about: Official English translation made at Mukden of Ordinance No. 23 regulating petroleum product import, export, sale, storage, and accounting forms.
subfiles.from: Jiro Minami, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to Manchukuo
subfiles.summary: Official translation of Kwantung Bureau Ordinance No. 23 promulgated by Ambassador Jiro Minami, establishing licensing, reporting, storage, and inspection regulations for petroleum trade in Kwantung and the South Manchuria Railway Zone, effective April 10, 1935. It defines controlled fuels, specifies administrative permits, details business succession and safety rules, prescribes penalties, and appends mandatory monthly reporting forms for oil receipts and deliveries.
subfiles.title: Kwantung Bureau Ordinance No. 23: Regulations for the Control of Petroleum Products
subfiles.to: Oil Dealers and Public, Kwantung Province and South Manchuria Railway Zone

subfiles.about: Summarizing statements by a Union Oil Company representative regarding crude sales to the monopoly and Mitsubishi's agency relationship with Associated Oil.
subfiles.from: W. T. T., Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: State Department memorandum summarizing Union Oil representative's statements on selling crude to the Manchurian monopoly through Japanese agents.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Union Oil Company Representative's Statements on Manchuria Oil Monopoly
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Reporting on an interview with H. R. Greatwood of Union Oil Company concerning sales to the monopoly, Japanese navy contracts, and local agency arrangements.
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Grummon reports conversations with Union Oil representative H. R. Greatwood regarding company operations, crude sales to the Dairen refinery via Nissho, navy supply contracts, and competitor sales.
subfiles.title: Visit of Representative of Union Oil Company to Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
